messages:
samuel: heads up — noticed a spike where a subset of EU SSE clients go into a 'probe -> hard backoff' loop and never rejoin. console shows repeated small delays then a quota-ish drop. not full 429s, just short-lived latency, then client gives up :confused:

Tess: repro steps? is this only SSE or also ws?

samuel: mostly SSE. reproduces on canary region eu-west-2. trace shows: server sends keepalive, client sends probe, server replies slowly (~900ms), client triggers our shepherd heuristic, increments backoff budget, then reconnects fail due to sticky routing to overloaded pool. no explicit 4xx.

kai: do we have samples in the console tagged as 'probe' events? iirc probes are sampled out so we might be missing visibility.

anya: console telemetry lagged by ~4–6m this morning while this happened, so the alerts didn't surface. i saw the events only after the canary finished. ops-bot also logged a canary-failure at deploy time.

samuel: attaching the small log snippet we saw in the proxy: ```
[2026-03-23T10:11:02Z] conn=abcd keepalive->sent
[2026-03-23T10:11:03Z] conn=abcd probe<-recv latency=912ms
[2026-03-23T10:11:03Z] conn=abcd shepherd=tripped budget=0.3 backoff=1.8s
[2026-03-23T10:11:04Z] conn=abcd route=eu-pool-7 sticky=true capacity=95%
```

Tess: that shepherd config looks pretty aggressive. what are the defaults now?

samuel: current defaults are: ```
sse:
  probe_window_ms: 300
  shepherd_threshold_ms: 500
  shepherd_backoff_multiplier: 1.8
  max_backoff_seconds: 8
```

kai: two quick asks: 1) can we mark probe-originated reconnects in the console UI so they don't get counted as user-initiated disconnects (affects quota attribution)? 2) increase sampling rate for probe events during canary rollout so we see the full picture in realtime.

anya: agree. also we should separate "shepherded" sessions in the latency dashboard with a tag (shepherd=true) so alerts can be tuned. right now the dashboard aggregates and hides small repeated trips as noise.

samuel: i'm worried about sticky routing pinning to nearly-saturated pools. suggestion: route fallback policy should prefer lower-latency available pools for reconnects while inside a shepherd window, even if that means breaking affinity briefly.

Tess: LGTM as a rollback-safe change if we gate it behind a feature flag for 24h. we can do a small A/B where 10% of reconnects use the relaxed-affinity policy.

kai: also propose tweak: add jitter to shepherd_backoff_multiplier and increase shepherd_threshold_ms to 700ms for EU canary. should reduce false positives from tail latency.

samuel: i'll open a PR with three changes: bump threshold to 700ms, add jitter to backoff, and add a temporary console flag to surface probe-originated reconnects. cc @deploy-bot for rollout.

deploy-bot: canary requested by samuel. rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows. tagging telemetry bucket: sse.shepherd.canary.

anya: once the PR lands, let's also patch the alerting rule to ignore 1xx/2xx probe reconnect spikiness for 20m windows; that will avoid noisy pages during the gradual rollout.

samuel: great. i'll include a dashboard patch and a tiny note in the rollout doc about "probe vs user disconnect" so support doesn't escalate prematurely.

kai: thanks. quick follow-up: can we add a metric for "shepherd_trips_per_min_per_region"? that'll help long-term tuning.

Tess: noted. one more UX ask — expose "probe_sampling_rate" on the console page so SREs can temporarily increase it for incident investigations without a deploy.

samuel: perfect. will track as separate tickets and link in PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
